_comment: What training produces — checkpoints, log stream, streaming metrics. Differs from infer/eval in that metrics are emitted continuously during a long run, not just at the end.

checkpoints._comment: Models saved during training. selection.best_by + direction tells /train-run and downstream stages which ckpt is canonical.

metrics._comment: Streamed during training. Two granularities — step (high-freq, e.g. loss/lr) and epoch (low-freq, used for ckpt selection). primary_metric drives 'best' decisions. log_format/log_path describe the SOURCE — what the training code itself writes. What every downstream script reads is the normalized stream at <RUN_DIR>/stream.jsonl, which is a fixed convention and deliberately has no field here. See references/run-mechanics.md -> "Metric stream".

normalize._comment: How the normalizer turns the source into records. group_by: 'step' | 'step+namespace' | 'step+wall_time'. Filled by /train-init after showing the user the observed tag/field list — there is no universally correct grouping, so this is a recorded decision, not a default to inherit silently. Affects record_types reconciliation, not ranking.

tracking._comment: WHERE THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S HISTORY LIVES — distinct from log_format/log_path above, which is how MLClaw reads THIS run. This block is what makes past runs retrievable: entity/project for wandb, tracking_uri + experiment for mlflow, log_dir for raw tensorboard. backend:"none" is a CONCLUSION (no tracking call anywhere in the code), not a gap — record it and stop looking. Reachability and missing credentials are NOT recorded here: provenance.json -> sources_checked owns that for every source, and duplicating it here would let the two drift. Record the locator even when unreachable — a locator you can't use yet is a todo. When pulling history, include failed runs (the only record of what the author ruled out) and bound the pull.
